# State Management Checklist: Feedback Sweep, slice 1 of 2 — the checkpoint

**Purpose**: Unit tests for the requirements governing sweep state — the
Feedback Sweep Log's lifecycle, the idempotency key, loop convergence, the
interrupt windows, and the single-store boundary. Validates how the
requirements are *written*, not whether an implementation works.

**Created**: 2026-08-20

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Feedback Sweep Log Lifecycle

- [x] CHK001 - Is the act that **creates** the `### Feedback Sweep Log` heading and header row specified, given the table does not exist before the first sweep? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK002 - Is it specified whether creating the table and writing its first row are **one write or two**, and that both ride the same FR-012a bookkeeping commit? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK003 - Are requirements defined for a workflow file that **already carries** a `### Feedback Sweep Log` heading — for example a file scaffolded by copying a prior feature's workflow — given the log is the sole idempotency key? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK004 - Is FR-013's placement anchor (`immediately after ### Consensus Resolution Log`) defined for a workflow file where that heading is **absent**? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK005 - Is the placement rule's **heading-level sensitivity** specified, given the anchor is written at `##` in part of the committed corpus and at `###` in the rest? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the assignment rule for the log's leading `#` column specified across **multiple runs and multiple bookkeeping commits**? [Resolved, Spec §FR-013a]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is it stated that the sweep reads the Feedback Sweep Log from the **local working tree** rather than from the remote, which FR-012e's recovery reasoning depends on? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012e]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the log's column semantics defined for every class, including which cells an `answered`, `deferred`, or `no action` row leaves empty? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the escaping rule for reviewer-derived prose in the `Disposition` cell stated with enough precision to be verified? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013, SC-010]

## Idempotency and the Skip Key

- [x] CHK010 - Is FR-009's "skip" **scoped** — does it remove the comment from classification only, or from the whole run — given FR-015b requires logged comments to stay visible to reconciliation? [Resolved, Spec §FR-009a]
- [x] CHK011 - Are requirements defined for a **new comment posted on an already-logged thread**, which carries a new id and must be handled as a new item? [Resolved, Spec §FR-009a]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is it stated that a logged id is skipped **regardless of whether the operator has resolved its thread**? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK013 - Are the consequences specified for a thread the operator resolves between runs, whose **subsequent comments** become invisible because FR-004 reads only unresolved threads? [Resolved, Spec §FR-009a]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is the skip key's behavior defined when the log holds a comment id the current observation does not contain? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is it unambiguous that a comment absent from the log is a candidate **even when a sweep reply to it already exists**? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK016 - Are requirements defined for a malformed or partially-written log row — one whose comment-id cell cannot be read — given a mis-read skip key silently re-processes or silently drops? [Resolved, Spec §FR-009a]

## Convergence and Termination

- [x] CHK017 - Is the **convergence invariant** stated as a requirement — that each run strictly reduces the set of trusted, unlogged, unexcluded comments or leaves it unchanged — rather than asserted only as a rationale? [Resolved, Spec §FR-006c]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the termination condition ("a run finds no trusted, unlogged comment") written as a requirement anywhere, or only implied by FR-018's proceed path? [Resolved, Spec §FR-006c]
- [x] CHK019 - Are requirements defined for an FR-011a human-review comment that **recurs on every run**, given it takes no class, writes no sweep row, and therefore never leaves the candidate set? [Resolved, Spec §FR-006c]
- [x] CHK020 - Is the operator action that breaks the FR-011a repeat cycle specified, given consensus is not proven deterministic and a re-run may disagree again? [Resolved, Spec §FR-006c, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK021 - Is it stated that the sweep's own replies never enter a later candidate set, tying FR-015's marker to FR-006's exclusion and FR-015b's appended comment id? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-015, §FR-015b]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is FR-006b's empty-account failure connected to the convergence claim — that the conjunction goes permanently false and **nothing** is excluded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006b]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is it stated that the operator resolving review threads is **not** a precondition for the run to proceed? [Completeness, Coverage]

- [x] CHK024 - Is the **reply timing** fixed — per handled comment immediately after its bookkeeping commit, or batched once at end of run — given FR-003 requires cross-platform determinism? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015c]
- [x] CHK025 - Do FR-015's run-scoped qualifier ("a run whose bookkeeping commits **all** landed") and FR-011a's sibling-replies-post rule agree on what a mid-run stop does to already-recorded items? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015c]
- [x] CHK026 - Are requirements defined for **two interrupt windows composing** — an early amendment fully recorded while a later amendment's push fails — naming whether the early item is left rowed-but-unreplied? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015c, §SC-013]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is each interrupt window's **terminal state after resume** stated explicitly, rather than left to be derived from the ordering rule? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012a, §FR-012e, §FR-015b]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are the two push-failure variants (amendment commit unpushed; bookkeeping commit unpushed) distinguished by their effect on the skip key? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012e]
- [ ] CHK029 - Is it specified what the FR-020 report's what-landed section must say when a stop occurs **between** an amendment commit and its bookkeeping commit? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-012e]
- [ ] CHK030 - Are requirements defined for a stop that occurs **after** some replies posted and before others, so the report's what-landed line is accurate per comment? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020]

## Remediation Record

about what answers them. Each `[Resolved, ...]` tag names the requirement that

This domain ran in two sittings. The first added FR-006c, FR-009a, FR-013a,
FR-015c, SC-012, and SC-013 to `spec.md` and stopped before marking its own
items or reconciling `plan.md`. The second sitting marked the items against the

requirements they cite, corrected one of them, and finished the plan alignment.
The `Closed in` column separates the two.

Marker names below are written unbracketed on purpose. Bracketed marker syntax
in a historical record is counted as a live marker by every marker counter that
reads this file, which would report a closed gap as open.

**The one correction sitting 2 made.** FR-015c closed with a blanket sentence
saying a run that stops for another reason still posts the replies it owes
first. Read against FR-015b's own definition of owed, that sentence covered the
FR-012e push-failure stop, where the two already-recorded comments **are** owed
replies at the moment the push fails — so it would have posted two replies into
the exact state FR-015c had just fixed at zero, and left the FR-020 what-landed
line naming replies that are not on the pull request. FR-015c now splits the
stops by where they sit relative to the reply point: FR-017 and FR-011a stop
after it and have already replied, and the other six stop before it and post
none. That is what CHK025 asks for, so CHK025 closes with it rather than
staying open beside a requirement written to answer it.

**Plan alignment.** `plan.md`'s Failure Paths section described the write order
as "amendment commit, push, then bookkeeping commit, then replies", which reads
as one repeating per-item cycle and is the per-item order FR-015c rules out. It
now states the two levels separately: the commit cycle repeats per amendment,
and replies come once at the end of the run after every bookkeeping commit has
landed.

**One item routes to consensus rather than being settled here.** FR-012a ends
"a run with no handled comments writes no rows and takes no bookkeeping commit",
and FR-013 defines handled as having been assigned a class. An FR-011a
human-review outcome takes no class, so it is not handled — yet FR-011a still
requires one Consensus Resolution Log row for it, and FR-012a's first sentence
requires Consensus Resolution Log writes to ride a bookkeeping commit. A run
whose only outcome is a human-review item therefore has a mandated row and no
commit named to carry it. Both requirements are settled work from earlier
passes and the fix is a cadence decision rather than a wording one, so it is
routed rather than taken unilaterally.

**Counting note.** The runner helper's gaps mode matches only the bare
single-word Gap marker. It reported **zero** against the sixteen this file
actually carried, because every one of them was a combined form. That is the
same blindness the security domain recorded at 4 of 8, at its limit: a helper
count of zero is not on its own evidence that a checklist is clean. The pattern
that matches the whole family is the bracket expression containing Gap anywhere
inside it.
